files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
The first release of Budget out of beta. Alongside the changes below there is now an Android app, Budget Companion, on [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.otherworld.budget).

### Added
- **The API can set a transaction's tags.** `POST` and `PATCH /api/v1/transactions` take `tag_ids`, with the same rules as the web UI: on your own account your global tags and the tags of the transaction's category, and on an account shared with you the owner's tags of the categories they share with you, which `GET /api/v1/tags` now lists as well. An edit's `tag_ids` replaces the whole set, a tag already on the transaction can always be sent back, and tags of the owner's that you can't use are left on. Changing a transaction's tags also moves its `updated_at`, and the response carries the new one, while sending back the tags it already has changes nothing. A tag that can't be used refuses an edit, while a new transaction is still recorded and the response says why in `tags_error`. `GET /api/v1/capabilities` gains `tag_ids_available`. Suggested by @SGiersch ([#420](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/discussions/420))
- **The API can read tags, filter the transaction list further, record transfers and mark a transaction reconciled.** Every transaction now carries its `tags`, an empty list when it has none, and `GET /api/v1/tags` lists your tags, each with the tag set and category it belongs to, as a category tag can only be put on a transaction in that category. `GET /api/v1/transactions` takes `type`, `status`, `reconciled`, `uncategorized`, `tagId`, `amountMin` and `amountMax`, and a value it cannot read is refused instead of ignored. `uncategorized=true` lists the transactions with no category, and `uncategorized=false` the rest, those with a category and split ones. `POST /api/v1/transactions` takes `transfer_account_id`, which records both sides of a transfer between two open accounts in the same currency and links them. The two are recorded together or not at all, so a transfer is never left with one side missing. `POST` and `DELETE /api/v1/transactions/{id}/reconcile` mark a transaction reconciled or unreconciled, the same as in the web UI; a transaction dated in the future can't be reconciled. `GET /api/v1/capabilities` gains `tags_available`, `reconcile_available` and `transfers_available`, and `transaction_filters`, which names every filter the list takes, for a client to check first, as an older server ignores a filter or a field it does not know. All of these are additions. Tags suggested by @SGiersch ([#420](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/discussions/420))
- **The API says when an account was last reconciled.** Each account in `GET /api/v1/accounts` gains `last_reconciled_at`, the time a reconciliation of it was last completed, in the same format as `updated_at`. It is `null` for an account that has never been reconciled. Suggested by @SGiersch ([#427](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/427))
- **An import folder.** Pick a folder in your Files under Settings, add a subfolder for each account, and a statement dropped into one is imported in the background, with no column mapping to do. Each subfolder is tied to one of your own accounts and, for CSV and spreadsheet statements, one of your saved import templates; OFX, QIF and camt files need no template. The file is then moved into an **Imported** folder beside it and you get a notification saying how many transactions came in and how many were already there. A file that can't be imported goes into **Failed** with the reason: columns the template expects that the file doesn't have, a file type that isn't a statement, or a batch that looks the wrong way round (income as spending), which is left for you to check on the Import page as an import can't be undone. Share a subfolder the usual Nextcloud way and other people can drop their statements in without opening Budget; the folder has to be in your own Files, not on external storage and not one somebody shared with you. Every row goes into the subfolder's own account: an Account column in the template is not used here, and a statement with transactions for several accounts, or in a different currency from the subfolder's account, goes into **Failed** to be imported from the Import page, where you choose the account for each. An account the file has no transactions for doesn't count, so a bank's file of all your accounts where only one had anything imports as normal. Files that are already in a subfolder when you add it, or when you move the import folder somewhere else, are left where they are until they change: save a new statement over one of them and it is imported like any other. Restoring a backup leaves the files already in the restored import folders alone too, and says how many. A file that stops Budget while it is being read is set aside in **Failed** the next time round rather than tried again, so one bad file can't hold up the import folders of everyone else on the server. It is checked every 15 minutes, and **Check now** does it straight away. A subfolder can instead **hold its files for review**: each one waits, you get a notification, and the Import page lists it under **Waiting for review**, where **Review** opens it in the usual import steps with the subfolder's template and account already chosen and **Skip** moves it to a Skipped folder. An account can't be closed while an import folder still posts into it. Suggested by @belze-bu ([#425](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/425))
- **Import Excel and LibreOffice spreadsheets.** Some banks only export a statement as `.xls` or `.xlsx`, which meant opening it and saving it as CSV first. Those files, and `.ods`, can now be picked on the import screen as they are. The sheet with the statement on it is read like a CSV, passing over a cover sheet or an account overview and any hidden sheets, so column mapping, saved templates, rules and duplicate checks work the same, and the bank's lines above the table (account holder, period and so on) are skipped. Dates are read from the cell itself rather than from how the spreadsheet displays them, so a date can't come out with the day and month swapped. An "XLS" that is really a web page saved by the bank works too. So does a CSV or tab-separated file saved with an `.xls` name. Suggested by @belze-bu ([#424](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/424))
- **Spending by Category can leave categories out.** Its settings now list your expense categories with a tick next to each, and unticking one takes it off that tile, along with its subcategories. The total and percentages cover what is left so they still add up to 100%, and a line under the total says how many categories are hidden. It only affects that tile, so reports and the other totals still count them, and duplicated tiles each keep their own list ([#413](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/413))
- **The Upcoming Bills tile can keep long-overdue bills.** The tile leaves out bills more than a week overdue so it doesn't fill up with old ones. Its settings now have **Show bills overdue for more than a week** to keep them, which is how the Bills page and the Android app list them.
- **Recurring income can be skipped.** Bills and transfers have a **Skip** button, however the Income page did not, so the only way past a payment that was not coming this time was to mark it received, which records a receipt that never happened. The Income page now has the same **Skip**: the expected date moves on one cycle without marking anything received or creating a transaction, and **Undo** in the notification that appears puts the old date back. Suggested by @SGiersch ([#396](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/396))
- **Import from Firefly III, YNAB, Actual Budget, Mint and Monarch Money.** Pick the app under Import Format and upload its export. Each account in the file is matched to one of yours by name or created, categories are created as needed (YNAB and Actual category groups become parent categories), reusing the one you already have with the same name even when it is a subcategory, such as Groceries under Food, and tags come across as well. Both sides of a transfer between two of your accounts are imported and linked, so they don't count as income or spending, and a Firefly III transfer between accounts in two currencies uses each side's own amount and currency. Importing the same export again adds nothing, even when you had brought it in before as a plain CSV with your own column mapping, as the rows already there show as duplicates. A row only counts as one of those when its date, amount and description or payee match, whatever order the file lists them in, so a different purchase that only shares a memo is still imported. A CSV whose columns match one of these apps is recognised when it is uploaded, and **Switching from another app?** on the import screen says where each app keeps its export. Tab-separated `.tsv` files can be imported too, which is what YNAB exports for currencies with a comma decimal.
- **Ready to Assign on the Budget page.** A new card shows the month's income less what the month's budgets give out, so you can see whether there is money still waiting for a budget or whether the budgets promise more than came in. It follows the month you pick. Amounts carried over by envelope budgets are left out, as that money was assigned from an earlier month's income.
- **A getting started checklist.** A new user used to land on a dashboard of empty tiles. They now get five steps (currency, default categories, an account, a statement or bank connection, and a first budget) which tick themselves off as they go, and the tiles come back once it is finished or dismissed. Anyone who already has data never sees it.
- **Try Budget with sample data.** An empty budget can be filled with sample accounts, transactions, bills and budgets from the checklist. A banner marks it as sample data on every page, and **Clear sample data** removes everything again while keeping your settings. `occ budget:seed-demo` uses the same data, now dated relative to today.
- **Reordering without dragging.** Categories can be moved with Alt+Up and Alt+Down, Alt+Right makes one a subcategory of the one above and Alt+Left moves it back out a level. On the unlocked dashboard each tile has Move earlier and Move later, and the accounts tile settings have Move up and Move down.
- **An account's transaction list works on a phone.** It shows as two-line cards like the main Transactions page, and tapping one opens it for editing.
- **Future transactions show the balance they will leave.** In an account's transaction list a scheduled transaction (a bill, income or transfer booked ahead, or anything dated after today) had an empty balance column. It now shows what the balance will be once it and the scheduled transactions before it have gone through, in smaller grey text so it isn't mistaken for money already there, and in red if it would take the account below zero. The Projected Balance at the top of the account page, which wasn't showing, now appears when it differs from today's balance. Suggested by @facluz ([#414](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/414))
- **A notification when someone adds a receipt to your transaction.** A receipt photo added by someone you share an account with is saved in your Files, so you now get a Nextcloud notification saying who added it.
- **A Full control permission for sharing.** Categories, Bills, Recurring Income, Savings Goals and Projects now have a third permission next to Read only and Read & Write. For bills, recurring income, savings goals and projects it lets the other person delete them as well as edit them. For categories it lets them change what Read & Write keeps with you, the type, parent, budget and report settings, and add subcategories, including moving categories around within your tree. A subcategory they add under one of your categories is yours, so it shows in the right place for both of you, and it is shared back to them automatically. Deleting a category stays with you, with one exception: they can delete a subcategory they added themselves while nothing uses it. On the Budget page a shared category now shows your budget for the month, including your adjustment for that month and your envelope carry-over, where before it only showed the category's plain budget. With Full control the other person can change it there too, and the change goes where yours would, into your adjustment if you made one for that month. Without Full control those controls are read-only, where before they looked editable and failed on save. Accounts and Import Rules keep Read only and Read & Write. Follows on from [#402](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/402)
- **Find the person to share with by typing their name.** The share form and the shared-expense contact form search Nextcloud users as you type a name, user ID or email, so they still work on servers that hide the full user list.
- **Rules can tidy up text.** Three new rule actions work on the description, vendor, reference or notes. **Change Case** switches a field to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case or Sentence case, **Replace Text** swaps one piece of text for another, and **Regex Replace** runs a regular expression over one field and writes the result into the same field or a different one, so a long bank description can be split out into a vendor and a reference, for example. `$1` in the replacement puts back what the first bracketed group matched. A regex that doesn't match leaves the target field alone, and it counts letters rather than bytes, so cutting text to a length never splits a letter such as "ü" in two. Contributed by @saviq-work ([#406](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/pull/406))
- **The API can show balances, what is left of the budget and the bills due, so a phone app can check as well as capture.** `GET /api/v1/budget/status` gives each budgeted category and the totals for a month, with the same figures the Budget page shows (every figure is the month's, with a weekly, quarterly or yearly budget counted as its share of the month, and `period_to_date` gives a quarterly or yearly budget's quarter or year so far), and `GET /api/v1/bills/upcoming` lists the bills that are overdue or due in the next 14 days (or however many `days` you ask for). Both include categories and bills someone has shared with you. A transaction now says which transaction is the other side of a transfer and lists the parts of a split one, where before a split came through as one uncategorised amount, and `GET /api/v1/transactions/{id}/splits` returns just the parts (none once a transaction is no longer split). `GET /api/v1/transactions/recent` gains the account, the category and a `type`, so a client can tell money in from money out. A shared account's balance in `GET /api/v1/accounts` is now as of today and converted to your base currency like your own accounts, as it used to count future-dated transactions. `GET /api/v1/capabilities` gains `check_available` for a client to check before using any of this. All of these are additions, with one change: a transaction always has a `splits` list now, empty when it isn't split, so to tell whether splits sent with a new transaction were accepted, check `splits_error` ([#407](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/407), [#408](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/408))
- **The API can edit and delete transactions.** `PATCH /api/v1/transactions/{id}` changes only the fields you send, `DELETE /api/v1/transactions/{id}` deletes one and `DELETE /api/v1/transactions/{id}/splits` undoes a split. They work the same way as the web UI, so balances are recalculated and a split's parts are rescaled when its amount changes. Where the web UI warns first, the API refuses with a 409 and an `error_code` instead: changing the amount, type or date of one side of a transfer, changing them on a reconciled transaction without `confirm_reconciled`, and giving a split transaction a category. Deleting one side of a transfer leaves the other as a plain transaction and returns its id. Splitting a transaction in an account shared with you also works over the API now, where it used to answer 404. `GET /api/v1/capabilities` gains `edit_available` for a client to check first. A negative amount is refused with `invalid_amount` when recording or editing a transaction, as it saved the transaction the wrong way round, and accounts and categories now include an `owner`, so an app can offer only the categories that work for an account shared with you. Splitting a transaction reports problems in the same `error` format as the other calls. Suggested by @SGiersch ([#412](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/discussions/412))
- **`occ budget:purge-deleted-users` clears up after users deleted before this version.** Deleting a Nextcloud user used to leave their Budget data behind, and this version removes it when the user is deleted, so the command is for anyone deleted before the update. Run on its own it lists what each deleted user left, table by table, without changing anything, and `--force` removes it. `--user` limits it to the users you name, and a user who exists is always left alone. A user from an external backend such as LDAP can look deleted while that backend is unreachable, so check the list before using `--force`.
- **Quick Add can take a receipt.** The Quick Add page has an **Upload receipt** button at the top of the form, which on a phone offers the camera as well as your photos and files, and the receipt is attached when you save. Before, a receipt meant saving the transaction and then opening it again in Budget to attach the photo. When your administrator has set up receipt scanning, **Read receipt** fills in the date, amount, description, vendor and category from the photo for you to check, the same as the Add Transaction dialog. The photo is only sent to be read when you press it, as receipt scanning can be a paid service away from your server. Receipts can only be attached in your own accounts, so with an account someone shared with you the page says so before you save. If the transaction saves but the receipt doesn't upload, the page says that too, so it isn't entered twice. Suggested by @rajbps ([#419](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/419))

### Changed
- **Translations.** German and French have been updated from Weblate, and an Italian translation has been started.
- **Weekly, quarterly and yearly budgets are measured over the month on the Budget page.** A weekly budget was measured over the week holding the 15th, so early in the month a gym budget of £20 a week showed nothing spent while the budget alerts showed this week's £10, and a yearly budget counted the whole year's spending, so a £400 car service in June sat in every later month's Spent card and left Remaining £400 short. Every category now counts the month's spending against its budget's share of the month (a weekly budget times 52 over 12, a third of a quarterly one, a twelfth of a yearly one), which is what Total budgeted already counted, and a parent adds its subcategories' budgets the same way. A quarterly or yearly category also shows how much of its quarter or year has gone, such as "£400.00 of £1,200.00 this year", and a budget set for another period shows its monthly share under the amount. The dashboard's Budget Progress and Budget Breakdown tiles and the budget export count budgets the same way, so on the current month they match the Budget page, where they compared a yearly £1,200 car budget, all of it, with one month's spending. Over a longer or shorter range each budget counts for the months the range covers, so a monthly £400 is £1,200 over three months and a yearly £1,200 is £300.
- **Arranging the dashboard works on a phone.** With the dashboard unlocked, each tile's toolbar (size, move, settings, hide) sat on top of the tile's title, so on a phone, where it never hides, titles were cut down to "Upco…" and it was hard to tell which settings button belonged to which tile. On touch screens the toolbar is now a strip across the top of the tile with the title under it. Tiles are reordered there with the toolbar's arrows rather than by dragging, so a swipe over a tile scrolls the page instead of being taken as a drag. Moving or resizing a tile on a phone leaves the layout you arranged on a wider screen as it was, as the phone keeps its own order. On screens narrower than 1200px a summary tile at the top (Net Worth, Income and so on) now moves straight away when moved by arrow or by dragging, where before the new order only showed after a reload. **Add Tiles** no longer sits under the Nextcloud menu button on a phone either.
- **On a phone, opening a transaction no longer brings up the keyboard.** Its form put the cursor in Amount, so the keyboard covered half of it when you only wanted to look. Adding a transaction still starts in Amount.
- **The Upcoming Bills tile shows bills shared with you.** It used to list only your own bills, while the Bills page and the Android app included shared ones. Shared bills now appear there too, and the tile's settings have **Exclude shared bills** to leave them out.
- **Deleting a shared bill, transfer or recurring income needs Full control.** Read & Write on bills, recurring transfers and recurring income used to let the other person delete them, unlike savings goals and projects, where only the owner could. Read & Write now means edit everywhere and Full control means edit and delete, so someone you shared bills or income with at Read & Write can no longer delete them. Set the section to **Full control** in the share's settings to give that back.
- **The sidebar matches the other Nextcloud apps.** The menu used its own taller rows, 44px high with a pill-shaped highlight, so it looked noticeably bulkier next to Files and the rest of Nextcloud and fewer pages fitted on screen before it had to scroll. It now uses Nextcloud's own sizes, 34px rows with the same spacing, text size and rounded corners, and the page you are on is shown the way Nextcloud 35 shows it, a light tint with a bar down the left side, in place of the solid blue fill. The search box and **Tools & Settings** have been brought in line as well, and the **Tools & Settings** label now lines up with the items under it.
- **The Transactions page works on a phone.** At phone width the table only had room for three columns, so it dropped the description and cut the amount off at the edge of the screen. Each transaction is now a two-line card, with the description and amount on the first line and the date, category and account under them. Tapping a card opens it in the edit form, as editing one small field in place is fiddly on a phone. On any screen size, Reconcile, Find Duplicates, Match All and Export have moved into a **⋯** menu beside **Add Transaction** so the buttons fit on one line next to the title, and the **⋮** menu on each row is a list with names instead of a strip of unlabelled icons. **Delete** is in that menu now rather than sitting on every row.
- **Amounts show a + or - sign.** The transactions table told income and spending apart by colour alone, which doesn't work for colour-blind users and was hard to read on the dark theme. Red and green amounts also use lighter shades on the dark theme.
- **Adding a transaction takes fewer clicks.** The form used to open on an empty "Choose transaction type" and "Choose an account", both required. It now starts on Expense, with Expense, Income and Transfer as three buttons, and picks the account the list is filtered to, or failing that the last account you saved a transaction to, or your only open account. The cursor starts in Amount and the date picker no longer pops open over the form. Receipts, notes and **Exclude from forecast** are under **More options**, which opens by itself when the transaction already uses them or when receipt scanning is set up.
- **Settings are saved as you change them.** There was one **Save Changes** button at the top of an eleven-section page, so a change near the bottom was easy to leave unsaved. Each setting is now saved as soon as it is changed, with a short "Saved" beside it (changing one several times in quick succession saves the last choice), and a row of buttons at the top jumps to each section. **Reset All to Defaults** has moved into the Danger Zone, away from where Save used to be.
- **The dashboard is less cluttered.** The "Dashboard is locked" line has gone, leaving the page title and a lock button, and the Pension and Assets cards are hidden while you have no pensions or assets. Tiles with nothing to show yet, such as Upcoming Bills with no bills, take half their height, and go back to full size once there is something in them or when the dashboard is unlocked to rearrange it. The saved layout is not touched by any of this. On a phone the summary cards sit two to a row, where before they filled the whole first screen. Recent Transactions shows five rows by default, which is what its settings already said it did, so neither it nor Spending by Category scrolls inside the page.
- **Charts are easier to read.** Curved lines no longer overshoot the real figures between months, the line into the current month is dashed with "(so far)" in its tooltip so a half-finished month doesn't look like a drop, and chart axes read £4K rather than £4,000.00.
- **Expenses and Income on the Budget and Categories pages are tabs.** They had a ✕ and a + on them, which looked like remove and add buttons. The budget table also grows with the page instead of scrolling inside it, and Total Spent no longer has a red ✕ for its icon.
- **Summary cards look the same on every page**, in the style of the dashboard's, and figures show "--" rather than "$0" until they have loaded.
- **The help button has moved to the bottom of the sidebar**, beside **Tools & Settings**. It used to float over the bottom right of the page, where it covered the delete button of the last transaction on screen.
- **Empty pages share one look**, and Accounts, Assets, Pensions, Savings Goals, Tags, Projects and Exchange Rates show a loading indicator instead of a blank page while their data loads.
- **Month names follow your Nextcloud language** instead of the browser's, now in charts and reports as well.
- **Only the owner of a shared account can delete it.** Anyone with write access could delete a shared account along with all of its transactions. People it is shared with no longer see the delete button.
- **The user picker for sharing follows your Nextcloud sharing settings**, including whether users can be listed at all, limiting to your own groups and "only share with group members".
- **Reports agree with each other.** Categories excluded from reports, or muted, were only left out when grouping by category, so the same month gave a different total grouped by month, vendor, account or tag, and in the Cash Flow, Category by Month and tag reports. Every grouping now leaves them out the same way, including the parts of split transactions filed under them, and transfers between your own accounts are left out of the category view as they are everywhere else. Income & Expenses now lists income by category, where it used to list your 15 biggest payers and leave the rest out of the total, and it has an Uncategorized row (as does spending or income grouped by category), so income you haven't filed yet still counts and Net matches Cash Flow. These reports also convert accounts in other currencies the way Cash Flow does, so they still agree when your accounts are in more than one currency.
- **Year over Year matches the other reports.** In the all-accounts view it counted both sides of every transfer as income and spending, along with pension payments, future scheduled transactions and excluded categories. It now uses the same figures as the Cash Flow report to the penny, converting accounts in other currencies the same way and keeping all of a crypto account's decimal places, and category spending has refunds taken off as the Budget page does.
- **Budget alerts, the budget status tile and applying rules to a lot of transactions are much quicker.** **Apply Rules** saves the changes 500 transactions at a time, and if the database refuses one, only that one is left unchanged. Its preview and its list of what changed show the first 500. The daily digest and bank sync are also spread over the cron runs one user and one bank connection at a time, so one slow bank no longer holds up everyone else.
- **Large ledgers are quicker to work with.** Importing a big statement reads the rules and the account's existing transactions once, where it read them again for every row. Exporting transactions to CSV is several times faster (63,000 transactions now take 2 to 3 seconds, where they took up to 22), deleting thousands of selected transactions at once is several times faster as well, and the transactions list gets the tags with the page rather than asking for each row's tags separately. Reports, Year over Year and the dashboard are quicker on long histories with accounts in more than one currency, as your base currency and exchange rates are read once rather than for every transaction, and Repair Data's **Scan for Issues** is quicker on long histories too. The page of an investment or crypto account no longer downloads and stores the same exchange-rate history again for each transaction, which could take 10 seconds or more.
- **Error and success colours, badges and chart labels are readable in the dark theme.**
- **A page that fails to load says so and offers Retry**, where it used to show an empty list with buttons that did nothing. An account whose transactions failed to load no longer says it has none.
- **Factory reset removes everything.** It left tag sets, interest rates, recurring pension contributions, debt scenarios, import templates, saved reports, the shares you granted, bank connections and transaction tags behind. Shares other people granted to you are kept.
- **Bank sync with SimpleFIN only connects to simplefin.org.**
- **Budget opens faster.** Reports, Forecast, Pensions, Assets, Import, Rules, Bills, Bank Sync, Exchange Rates and Projects are now loaded the first time you open them rather than all at once, which cuts the download when the app starts by about a quarter.
- **An account's transaction list shows the same details as the Transactions page**, including the pending, not in forecast and pension badges and the reference, and a transfer's label is translated in both.
- **Import History lists your imports.** The tab was always empty. It now shows each import's date, account, number of transactions and the dates they cover. The Download and Rollback buttons have gone, as there was nothing to download and rolling back never removed anything.
- **The Skip Duplicate Transactions switch has gone from Settings.** It never did anything: duplicates are skipped on import unless you tick **Import flagged duplicates too** on the import screen.
- **Reconciliation History shows the latest two.** An account's page listed every reconciliation, up to 20, above its transactions. It now shows the two most recent, with **Show all** under them for the rest and **Show fewer** to fold them away again. Two or fewer show as before. Suggested by @SGiersch ([#418](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/418))

### Fixed
- **The API and Convert to transfer no longer post into a closed account.** The API accepted a transaction for a closed account, and **Convert to transfer** could make one the other side of a transfer, which left the account holding money it was closed without. Both are now refused until the account is reopened, and the API answers `account_closed`.
- **Messages are readable on Nextcloud 32 and later.** The Quick Add page's messages and the pop-up notifications in the corner of the page used Nextcloud's new pale error and success colours for their text, so on a white page they were close to invisible.
- **A camt file with a statement for each day counts every day.** When a file held several statements for the same account, the import screen's summary for that account counted only the last one's transactions.
- **Deleting an account forgets which OFX and QIF accounts were imported into it.** The remembered routing was left behind pointing at an account that no longer existed, and went into backups that way.
- **The receipt pickers only offer files that can be attached.** They offered any image, so a GIF or BMP was only refused once the transaction had been saved. An iPhone photo is still handed over as a JPEG, which receipt scanning can read.
- **A transaction marked unreconciled can be reconciled again.** Marking a reconciled transaction unreconciled left it tied to the statement it had been reconciled against, so it could not be ticked when you reconciled a later statement, and nothing said why. It now leaves that statement, and the change is written to the audit log.
- **An investment account's figures no longer draw over its name.** The top of an investment account's page has five figures, and when they didn't fit beside the account name they were drawn over it, its type and its status dot, which was worse with longer translations such as German. The figures now move onto a row of their own when there isn't room, and wrap onto more lines if they still don't fit. Reported by @SGiersch ([#423](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/423))
- **An income category's details show its income as positive.** Category Details showed the total and average of an income category as negative, so a €1,000.00 salary read as -€1,000.00 under **Total Spent**, while the chart and This Month beside it showed €1,000.00. They are now positive, the total is labelled **Total Income** and the chart **Monthly Income**. Reported by @SGiersch ([#422](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/422))
- **Quick Add's drop-down lists no longer cut off the bottom of their text.** The account, type and category fields were a few pixels too short for the text in them, so the bottoms of the letters were lost. Every field on the page is now the same height, and tall enough for its text.
- **Quick Add shows apostrophes in its messages.** In a language that uses them, the Save button and the error messages showed a code in place of each apostrophe, so in French the button read `Enregistrer l'opération` after every save.
- **The dashboard's budget tiles work again.** The Budget Progress tile drew its bars with no height, so they never showed, and went back to the current month, all accounts and shared accounts included after every reload, whatever its settings said. The Budget Breakdown tile left its Category column empty, and the Budget Health tile always showed "--" instead of how many budgets are on track.
- **Editing a transfer shared with you no longer clears its category.** A transfer whose category wasn't shared with you opened with "No category", and saving it, even unchanged, removed the category from the owner's transfer. One into or out of an account that wasn't shared with you couldn't be saved at all. Both are now kept as they are, as bills and recurring income already did, and a transfer paying a card you can't see keeps its statement or minimum-payment amount.
- **Receipt scanning through the Otherworld relay uses its new address.** The relay moved to api.otherworld.dev and the old ocr.otherworld.dev address no longer answers, so scans and the subscription links failed to connect.
- **A category added after a month's budget adjustment can be budgeted in that month.** An adjustment keeps a copy of every category's budget from when it was made, so a category created afterwards had none, and changing its budget for that month failed with "No budget snapshot found". Saving it now adds the category to the adjustment, starting from the budget the page was showing, and leaves the other categories alone. Contributed by @almeidandres ([#416](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/pull/416))
- **Bills, transfers and income show the right paid state and dates.** A bill's paid state was judged by calendar month or by its last payment date, and each page worked out dates its own way, so the Bills page, the Transfers page, the Bills Calendar and the dashboard could disagree. A custom bill could jump a year ahead, a one-time bill with no month landed on 1 January next year with an empty Due Date, income read Received beside a date still to come, and editing a bill after paying it put it back on the payment it had just made. Bills, transfers and income now follow one schedule: the next date is the first payment not yet made, received or skipped, paying settles exactly that payment, and an edit that leaves the schedule alone leaves the date alone. A bill with no due day or month set keeps the day and month of its start date when it is paid, skipped or auto-paid, and a bill or income set up before this version whose next date was saved on the 1st or in January counts that date as the payment for its month, quarter or year, rather than being paid again on its start date's day. A twice-monthly bill or income on the 13th to 15th that was due on the 28th isn't paid again a couple of days later. Reported by @TerjeTM ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **A bill is paid once.** An imported statement now replaces a payment you had already marked, or auto-pay had booked, instead of adding a second one. That works for every one of the bill's payments the statement holds, in whatever order it lists them, and a split with a contact, receipts, tags and notes on the payment move to the bank's transaction. A payment you have reconciled is left as it is, and the bank's transaction for it isn't used to pay the next one instead. A double click creates one bill, transfer or income, and paying from a page left open on an old date is refused with "Reload the page" rather than paying the next one. Linking a bank transaction to a bill pays it properly or not at all, and a deleted bill's old payments can be matched to a new bill. An imported withdrawal for a recurring transfer already marked paid replaces that payment rather than also paying the next one, and payments added with **Record transaction** before this update don't come back in the unrecorded payments card.
- **A bill's pre-booked transaction stays pending until the bill is paid.** The background job booked it on its due date while the bill was still unpaid, so the money left the balance once then and again when the bill was paid. The update puts those rows back to pending, and so does restoring a backup made by an earlier version, leaving alone a payment recorded with **Record transaction** after paying a cycle late. Rows in an account that has since been deleted are left as they are, so they can't stop a bill being deleted, a factory reset or a deleted user's data being removed.
- **Mark Unpaid undoes the whole payment.** It also removes a transaction added with **Record transaction**, puts back the pre-booked transaction a linked bank transaction replaced, removes both sides of a transfer the app booked, while a transaction that came from your bank is kept and only unlinked, and warns before deleting a payment reconciled against a statement. Mark Unpaid and Mark Unreceived also survive a backup restore. The **Undo** in each notification on the Bills, Transfers and Income pages undoes the action it was shown for, where an older one could revert a later payment instead.
- **Recurring transfers book both sides.** Paying one always credits the destination account and converts between currencies when the two accounts differ, including when it is paid from the bank's own withdrawal. A transfer between currencies that 2.54 had already booked ahead is converted when it is paid as well, where it would have credited the same number in the other currency. It can be paid by the bank's own pair of transactions, and when the destination account's statement is imported or synced, the bank's credit takes the place of the deposit the app booked, whichever statement comes in first, however the transfer was paid and even when the bank credits it a few days later, so the money doesn't arrive twice. Within one currency it has to be the same amount, between two currencies within 10% of the converted amount (banks use their own rate and fees), and a credit that matches one of your recurring incomes, such as a salary of the same amount, is never taken for it. With no exchange rate the transfer can't be paid from a bank transaction. A deposit you have reconciled is kept. A salary and a rent bill are no longer paired up as a transfer. Paying a card in another currency by its statement, balance or minimum payment converts the amount taken from your account, where it took the card's figure as it was. A **Minimum payment** transfer to a card with no minimum payment set is now refused, where it paid 0.00 every month and showed as paid.
- **Recurring income.** One receipt settles one payment and is dated the day it arrived, an imported payment marks the income received and takes the place of a credit already booked for it, keeping its category, receipts, tags and notes, and undo removes only the income's own credit. Detect Income stops offering income you already track, puts what it finds on the right day and always gives it a name.
- **Dates follow your timezone.** Overdue, due today, this month's counts, balances as of today, reports and the Nextcloud dashboard widget used the server's date, which is UTC. So for the first hours of each day east of Greenwich, and every evening west of it, they were a day out: a purchase made after midnight in Sydney was missing from the balance until midday, and a bill due today in Los Angeles showed as overdue in the evening. They now use your Nextcloud timezone, and scheduled transactions clear within the hour of the account owner's midnight. A reconciliation adjustment made in the evening west of Greenwich is no longer dated tomorrow, which kept the reconciliation from finishing. The budget tile, budget alerts, unusual spending alerts, the API's budget status, an account's This Month figures, Year over Year, the digest and the scheduled monthly report follow your date as well, so they no longer show last month on the morning of the 1st east of Greenwich.
- **Auto-pay and reminders.** Auto-pay is due by each bill's own date, where a weekly bill only auto-paid once a month. A weekly or fortnightly bill that fell behind because of that pays every missed payment in one go after the update, each dated on its own due date, and uses the bank's transaction for any of them already imported from a statement rather than booking a second payment beside it. A bill whose auto-pay couldn't record the payment is put back and reported, instead of moving on with nothing booked, and two auto-pay runs at the same time pay a bill once without switching its auto-pay off. Reminders go out once per due date, with one overdue notice if the bill is still unpaid after it, so a weekly bill paid a day late still gets the next week's reminder.
- **Card holds from bank sync.** A bill paid by a hold stays paid once, by the payment that posts. A cancelled hold no longer leaves its bill paid, a posted payment takes the bank's final amount and description, it no longer takes over another merchant's hold, and holds still post or clear after **Include pending** is turned off.
- **Amounts are in the right currency.** Bills, transfers, income and their notifications show amounts in their account's currency, and the Monthly Total cards convert them to your base currency, where euros were added to pounds. Detected bills and split remainders show in the account's currency too.
- **Detect Bills** stops offering bills and transfers you already have, puts what it finds on the right day and always gives it a name.
- **The Bills Calendar follows the same schedule as the Bills page**, the dashboard's bills and income tiles follow their settings, and the daily digest counts every bill due and lists overdue bills separately. The calendar says why an account shared with you has no projected balance.
- **Bills on shared accounts.** A bill on an account someone shared with you books its payments as the account's owner, and a split bill there uses categories the owner can see. A shared account's page shows its tiles and balance chart, and a shared card's Payment due tile counts the other person's payment.
- **One-time bills whose date was made up are flagged.** A one-time bill saved without a month, before the Due Date field existed, was given a date by the server: 1 January next year, or the invoice's day in the following year. As that can't be told apart from a real date, these bills now show **Check date**, and the edit form says the date was filled in, until you pick one and save.
- **Categories and tags.** Deleting a category takes it off bills and recurring income, and asks first when a scheduled payment uses it. A delete that is refused leaves the category's subcategories as they were, where it could already have deleted them along with their budgets and tags. Transactions left filed under a category deleted earlier counted in balances but in no category, not even Uncategorized; the update makes them Uncategorized. A deleted tag no longer follows a bill's payments.
- **Pensions.** A contribution counts in the pension's balance straight away. A scheduled contribution keeps its day of the month, posts one missed date at a time, shows as overdue when it is due, and when it can't post it stops and tells you, with the amount in the pension's currency. Deleting an entry keeps a bank transaction that came from your statement, and warns when its bank transaction was reconciled. A payment from an imported account is counted once, deleting a pension leaves its bank transactions out of spending, and balance history and the projected balance count scheduled contributions. An account name with an & in it shows properly on a scheduled contribution, and an imported payment is only taken as a pension contribution when it names the pension or its provider as a word of its own, or has no category and is within a few days.
- **Repair data no longer deletes real bill payments** or drops payments still owed. Payments an earlier Repair switched to scheduled are put back by the update.
- **Backups.** A restore keeps what you share and bills on shared accounts, and a restored bill keeps its split categories, reminders and due date. A dismissed unrecorded payment stays dismissed. Bank connections, import rule groups, rules that add tags or match on an account, and the account and tag filters of saved reports come back pointing at your restored data, where bank sync stopped and those rules and filters were lost, and so do the dashboard's tile filters, hidden categories and account order and your muted budget alerts. When a bank account's link to Bank Sync can't be matched to an account in the backup, the restore tells you, so you can choose the account again in Bank Sync. Undoing a pension schedule's last post after a restore no longer posts it twice. A damaged or hand-edited backup is refused with a message naming the file and nothing is changed, where it failed part way with a server error. Backups made by this version are marked as a newer format, so an older version of Budget warns before restoring one.
- **Reports, budgets and forecasts.** The forecast no longer counts transfers between your accounts as income and spending. Auto budgets count the bills that will show as spent, in the month shown. Budget alerts, the budget tile and the digest measure spending only, over every account you can see, and income targets are kept out of budget totals. A budget on a subcategory of a category set to **Exclude from reports** is left out of budget alerts, the dashboard's budget tiles, the Nextcloud dashboard widget and the digest, as it is on the Budget page, and the dashboard's Budget remaining counts a weekly or yearly budget's share of the month, where it counted the whole budget against the one month. A tag-linked savings goal counts the tagged transfers that feed it and takes off the ones out of savings, and the account page's This Month tiles count only what happened.
- **Transactions.** A bill's payment can't be set back to scheduled, deleting a scheduled transaction no longer says it changes the balance, and a scheduled payment can't be ticked into a reconciliation. Deleting an account switches off the bills that use it.
- **Splitting a transaction again can't lose its split.** A new split with a 0.00 part, or a part that wasn't a number, was refused only after the old parts had been deleted, so the transaction was left with some of its parts or none. Every part is now checked first, and a refused split changes nothing.
- **Create default categories no longer adds import rules that do nothing.** It added six rules with no category, which matched descriptions containing words like "shell" or "amazon" and then stopped your own rules from running, so the transaction stayed uncategorised, and the getting started checklist now offers it to every new user. Each default rule now files into its default category (a rule whose category isn't there isn't created), the ones still as setup left them are switched off by the update and when they come back from an older backup, and default rules now have priority 0 while a new rule starts at 1, so a rule you make runs before them. Their patterns match whole words, so a bookshop such as Waterstones isn't filed as a water bill, or "Mobile" as a petrol station.
- **Import rules made before 2.28 categorise imports again.** Since 2.28 a rule that hadn't been opened in the rule editor since, or that came back from an older backup, matched nothing when a statement was imported or a bank synced, and only worked from **Apply Rules** on the Rules page. They categorise imported and synced transactions again, and a rule with nothing it can do there, such as one with no actions or only a deleted category, no longer stops the rules after it.
- **Restoring a backup keeps cards and loans on the right side of zero.** A card or loan whose balance had crossed zero since it was opened, such as a card paid off past its balance or a loan opened in credit that now owes, came back on the wrong side with a wrong opening balance, which also moved net worth. It now comes back as it was.
- **Large backups export.** A backup of a big ledger, from around 110,000 transactions, ran the server out of memory and failed. The export is now built a little at a time and downloads as it is written, and holds the same data as before.
- **Saved reports work again.** Since 2.33.0 the **Saved reports…** menu showed blank entries and choosing one loaded nothing. They show their names and load their settings again.
- **Budgets, the forecast and the digest convert other currencies.** Spending in an account in another currency was added to the Budget page's Spent, budget alerts, the budget report, the dashboard's spending and budget tiles and envelope carry-over as if it were in your base currency, and the forecast added up balances in different currencies the same way. They are now converted at your exchange rates as the Cash Flow report does, on the dashboard from the moment the page loads rather than only after a tile's settings change, and Ready to Assign and the API's budget status use the same figures. The forecast leaves out an account with no exchange rate, as the dashboard does. The digest's income and spending now match the Cash Flow report too, with transfers between your own accounts left out.
- **Forecast warnings only come from a forecast with enough behind it.** The forecast counted the month in progress as a whole month and drew a straight line through as few as two months, so a new user could be warned of a negative balance on a few days of data, with a salary not yet paid this month projected to stop altogether. The forecast now learns from the twelve complete months before this one, only follows a trend once it has three of them and never projects income below the recurring income you have set up, and the warning waits until the forecast is reliable. Projected spending follows its trend only when it is rising: when your spending has been falling, the forecast assumes you keep spending your average, and never less than your bills, where a falling trend could project no spending at all. A steady history that really is heading below zero still warns.
- **Envelope budgets carry over what the Budget page showed as left.** A refund, or a transfer filed under the category on both sides, was ignored, so a refunded purchase counted in full and a monthly transfer to savings overspent the envelope every month.
- **Closing an account.** A bill or income set up by someone who can no longer post into the account, because the share ended or is read-only, stopped it being closed for good, and the message listed other people's items by name. Those are now ignored and let go of the account when it closes, with a bill's auto-pay switched off, and the message only names your own items. An account with a transaction booked in it for a later date can't be closed either, which the check missed when the transaction was a scheduled one.
- **Splitting, tagging, bulk editing and reconciling in an account shared with you.** With Read & Write you can now split and unsplit its transactions, tag them, and bulk edit, delete or reconcile them, where they failed with "Transaction not found" and the split form opened empty. You can reconcile the account itself and see its reconciliation history, interest and valuation too, where starting a reconciliation showed a database error and the history didn't load, and anyone the account is shared with can read that history. With Read only you can see a transaction's split parts, and opening a transaction no longer shows errors for its receipts or tag sets.
- **Reconcile started from an account's page lists only that account.** It opened the transactions list before its filters were filled, so the account filter was dropped and every account's transactions showed, and ticking one from another account did nothing.
- **Editing something shared with you no longer removes the owner's tags.** The bill and savings goal forms only show the tags and accounts you can see, so saving a shared bill took the owner's own tags off it and a shared goal lost its tag and account. Tags and links you can't see now stay as they are, and the same goes for a transaction's tags in a shared account and the tags a shared import rule adds.
- **Reports work for an account shared with you.** The Summary report failed and Cash Flow came back empty when you picked one, and so did dashboard tiles set to one.
- **Shared expenses.** Splitting a transaction from a shared account 50/50 or with one person stored no currency, so it showed in US dollars and the person's details left it out, and the update corrects the ones already made. Settling several splits at once recorded the whole payment against the first person, and now records each person's. A split whose transaction has been deleted, or is in an account you can no longer see, is listed under its note or "Shared expense" with its own amount, where it counted in the balance without being listed. Another user's contact, split or settlement answers "not found" rather than a server error, and across the app a request for something that doesn't exist no longer writes an error to the Nextcloud log.
- **Statement imports.** Two identical transactions in one QIF file are both imported, where the second was taken as a duplicate of the first. A CSV row whose description runs over more than one line is no longer dropped, an amount written as "45.00 DR" imports as money out, and a Category column files rows under the category you already have with that name, even when it is a subcategory, where it created a second one at the top level. The column can also give the whole path, such as "Food > Groceries" in a Skrooge export, which files the row under Groceries in Food and adds any level that is missing, where the whole cell became one category with that name. A category you already have named with the whole path still gets its rows, and a refund goes in the expense category it names, where it made an income category of the same name ([#421](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/discussions/421)). An amount with more than three decimal places, as crypto and investment exports have, was read as thousands, so "117.50000000" came in as 11,750,000,000, and it now imports correctly. A file imported before with those wrong amounts may bring its rows in again with the right amount, so delete the wrong ones. The review step shows each row in its account's currency and decimals, where a crypto import read "£0.00" and an OFX card in dollars showed pounds.
- **Unticking Apply import rules for categorization on the import screen leaves rules out.** The box was ignored, so rules still ran on the preview and the import. It now works, and for each new file it starts from the **Auto-apply Import Rules** setting.
- **The transactions list's Total gives one figure per currency.** With accounts in more than one currency on screen it added them together as if they were one currency. It now shows a total for each.
- **Unticking Split across categories unsplits a transaction.** Editing a split transaction, unticking the box and picking a category said "Transaction updated" and changed nothing. It now unsplits it into the category chosen, and split transactions opened from an account's page show their parts too.
- **A double click on Save creates one item.** A double click, or Enter pressed twice, could save a new transaction, account, category, rule, tag, contact, settlement or other item twice.
- **The Budget page's figures update straight away and add up to the penny.** Remaining, progress, the parent's total and the summary cards kept the old figure after you typed a budget, until the page was reloaded. Remaining also came out a penny short when budgets of different periods were mixed, and a budget spent exactly showed -0.00.
- **The Accounts page fits a phone again.** It showed three cut-off columns with Net Worth off the edge of the screen, and now shows the summary row and one column of accounts. The Budget page's column header, the Categories toolbar, the bill and income buttons and the Help page's system table fit as well.
- **Items shared with you read-only don't offer to change them.** They still showed Edit, Delete, Duplicate, Match transfer, Mark Paid, Mark Received and Skip, which the server then refused. Those are hidden now, along with Edit, Reconcile, Add Transaction and Import on an account shared with you read-only, and a shared transfer's Delete only shows with Full control, as a bill's does.
- **The API answers properly in a few more cases.** A transaction refused because its account was read-only or unknown held on to its idempotency key, so retrying the same draft on the right account failed with `request_in_flight` for a week, and it now records. Recording into an account you can't see says "Account not found" (404) rather than calling it read-only. A list sent where one value belongs is refused with a 400 when recording or editing, where a list sent as the vendor was saved as the text "Array" and one sent as the account recorded into the wrong account. `GET /api/v1/transactions` clamps `limit` again on Nextcloud 35, where 0, a negative number or anything over 500 got an empty error, and the info call answers at `/api/v1/` as well, which is where the API description sends generated clients, and they got a 404. Amounts are given in their currency's own decimal places, at least two, so 0.015 BTC no longer reads 0.02 and an app that sent a transaction back to change its description no longer changes its amount.
- **Upgrading from Budget 2.1.0 or older on Nextcloud 35 no longer stops with an error part way through.**
- **Share invitations go away once answered.** Accepting, declining or leaving a share left the invitation in your notifications.
- **A Budget result in Nextcloud's search opens the transactions it found.** Following one opened the whole Transactions list. It now opens filtered to the search, with the Filters panel showing it.
- **The account form keeps what you type.** A new account's starting balance went back to 0.00 when you changed its currency, its type or the in credit box, and Edit Account showed the previous account's values while it loaded, so an edit made in that moment was lost.
- **Debt Payoff shows the right figures.** Its Monthly Payment and each debt's minimum always read 0, and debts in other currencies were added up as if they were in your base currency, so a dollar card was counted as pounds. The totals are now converted as on the Accounts page, with each debt's own balance shown beside it. The plan also pays the same amount every month: when a debt is paid off, its minimum payment goes on to the next one, as a snowball or avalanche should, where the freed payment was dropped and the debt-free date came out years late.
- **Decimal Places set to 0 shows amounts without decimals.** The preview in Settings showed it, however the rest of the app kept two places. Amount fields still take decimals when you type them.
- **A budget cycle with a start day no longer loses a day next to the clocks going forward.** In London with the start day on the 30th, spending on 29 March fell into no cycle at all.
- **Account tiles draw their balance trend line, and the Institution field suggests banks again.** The trend line never drew, and the Institution field on the account form never showed its suggestions, and picking one did nothing. An account's balance trend and the dashboard's one-account chart now end at today's balance, where they ran a day behind.
- **Quick Add shows subcategories under their parent.** Its category list was flat, so two subcategories with the same name, such as Other under Food and Other under Travel, looked identical. Subcategories are now listed indented under their parent category, the way the main app's category pickers show them. Reported by @fatino ([#409](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/409))
- **No more false JavaScript-Format errors in Weblate.** Five strings with a percentage in them, like "{percent}% of what is already in {account}", were marked as printf-style strings, because "% o" looks like a format code. Weblate then flagged good translations such as German "{percent}% der" as broken. They are now marked as plain strings, so the error goes away and translations need no change. Reported by @SGiersch ([#415](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/415))
- **The Bills page cards count bills shared with you.** Due this month, Overdue, Monthly total and Paid this month only counted your own bills, although the list under them included shared ones, so a shared bill that was overdue was listed while the Overdue card said 0.
- **On a phone a form's title no longer hides under the Nextcloud header.** In Firefox on Android the edit transaction form, and other forms like it, could open with their title behind the header bar. Forms now open in the space below the header.
- **A link to one transaction opens it.** A link ending in `#transactions?id=` followed by a transaction number, which the Android companion app opens when you tap a transaction, now opens that transaction's edit form, where before it only showed the list. Opening or duplicating a transaction that wasn't in the loaded list failed with an error in the same way, and now works.
- **A shared account shows the same balance for both of you.** On the Accounts page your own accounts leave out future-dated transactions, however an account someone shared with you showed its stored balance, which counts them, and wasn't converted to your base currency. So a joint account with next week's rent already entered showed less for the person it was shared with than for its owner. Shared accounts are now worked out the same way as your own, on the dashboard, in net worth and in the forecast as well.
- **A very small crypto balance no longer breaks pages.** An account holding less than 0.0001 of a coin, or a rounding leftover in its future-dated transactions, made the whole Accounts page fail to load, along with the account's own page, the dashboard totals, the Nextcloud dashboard widget and the API's account list.
- **Adding a subcategory under a shared category gives a clear answer.** Categories shared with you were offered as a parent when adding a category, however only the owner can add subcategories to one, so saving failed with a raw database message. Shared categories are no longer offered as a parent, and moving or dragging your own category under a shared one is refused with "Only the owner can add subcategories to a shared category". Where you and the person sharing with you both have a category with the same name, the parent list also now offers your own category, where before it could pick theirs. Editing a shared rule to use a category the rule's owner can't see now says that, in place of "invalid category ID". Reported by @belze-bu ([#402](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/402))
- **The rules list shows a Set description badge.** A rule whose action sets the description showed no badge for it in the list, so it looked like the rule did nothing. Contributed by @saviq-work ([#405](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/pull/405))
- **Import rules accept every regex the server can run.** The rule builder checked regex patterns in the browser, whose regex engine is not the one rules run with, so valid patterns such as `(?i)` inline flags were refused. Patterns are now only checked when the rule is saved, and a bad one is refused with the reason rather than a general "Failed to save rule". A pattern can also be written as `/pattern/flags` to set its own flags, for example `/^ORDER-\d+$/` to match case-sensitively, where a plain pattern still ignores case. Contributed by @Saviq ([#403](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/pull/403))
- **A bill due on the 1st keeps its date after being paid early.** Paying a bill ahead moves its next due date on, but for a monthly, quarterly or yearly bill due on the 1st of the month, any later edit to the bill, even just renaming it, put the due date back to the next 1st as if it had never been paid.
- **The Category by Month report adds up.** Transactions with no category were left out of it altogether, so a month's Net total didn't match the same month on the other reports. They now have an **Uncategorized** row at the bottom, which also counts the parts of a split transaction with no category, and the rows add up to the Net total. Categories shared with you have their own rows as well. It's in the CSV and PDF exports too.
- **Dialogs close when you leave the page.** Going to another page with the browser's Back button left an open dialog on top of the new page. The dialogs the app builds as it goes, the duplicates finder and the transfer form among them, also ignored Escape and let the keyboard wander behind them, and most dialogs were hidden from screen readers while open.
- **Buttons on the Sharing and Bank Sync pages are styled.** Accept, Invite, Revoke, Leave and Disconnect used button classes the app never defined, so they showed as plain browser buttons.
- **Switching Categories between Expenses and Income no longer clears the selected tab on the Bills, Budget and Transfers pages.**
- **The "Budget adjusted from" message named the previous month** for anyone west of Greenwich, and a savings goal's target date could show the day before, as both read the date as UTC. The target date now follows your date format setting as well.
- **The Overdue card on the Bills page showed an empty circle**, along with a few other icons the app asked Nextcloud for under names it doesn't have.
- **Cards and column headers can be used from the keyboard.** Account, asset, pension and contact cards, the category tree, rule groups and sortable columns can be reached with Tab and opened with Enter, and icon buttons and fields that had no name for screen readers now have one.
- **The Rules page no longer scrolls sideways.** The sort arrow for the rule list picked up the transactions table's styling, which placed it absolutely, so it was drawn at the far right edge of the page instead of beside its column heading and made the page 2px wider than the window.
- **Icon buttons have names for screen readers.** Around 80 icon-only buttons (edit, delete, close and the like) were named only by their tooltip, which touch screens never show and some screen readers skip. The dashboard's tile size buttons now read Extra small, Small, Medium and Large in your language, where they were in English only.
- **Changing a credit card's statement day now saves.** It was only stored when the account was created.
- **Crypto balances keep all 8 decimal places** when a scheduled transaction clears or a backup is restored, where they were rounded to 2, and so do an account's running and projected balances and the parts of a split transaction when its amount changes. A yen split's parts are rounded to whole yen.
- **Tags created inside a category are included in backups.** They were never recorded against their owner, so since 1.0.44 they were left out of backups and restores and survived a factory reset. The update fixes existing tags, but a backup made before updating still lacks them, so make a new backup once you have updated.
- **Restoring a backup works on PostgreSQL.** It failed with "invalid input syntax for type boolean" whenever the backup held tags or other yes/no settings. A restore also keeps each account's wallet address, interest settings and last reconciled date, which were being reset, and restoring over existing data no longer leaves orphaned receipt links behind.
- **Transaction search works on Nextcloud 30.** It used a function added in Nextcloud 31 and failed with an error.
- **Rules with an "is between" condition made in the rule builder now match.** They never matched anything as the range was saved as text. Existing rules start working without being saved again, a range can start at 0, and a quote mark in a condition no longer breaks the rule editor.
- **A report filtered by tags no longer counts a transaction twice** when it has two of the chosen tags.
- **Report totals no longer show leftovers such as 0.30000000000000004.**
- **Budget carryover no longer counts a split transaction that pays into a pension as spending.**
- **Names containing "&" or quotes no longer show as "B&Q"** in some labels, tooltips and warnings.
- **Buttons that only appeared on mouse hover** can be reached by keyboard and on touch screens.
- **Screen readers announce** the form fields that had no label, the transfer link in transaction lists, and budget progress including when a budget is overspent.
- **Dates using a month name no longer garble months containing "j" or "d"**, such as French "janv.".
- **An error during bill auto-pay no longer stops the reminder job** for everyone else.
- **Forecast month labels and pension chart dates** follow your language and date format instead of showing in English.
- **Some bulk actions and settings switches said they had worked when the server had refused them.** They now show the error.
- **The rules list showed "No actions" for every rule made in the rule builder.** It now shows each rule's category, vendor, tags and other actions.
- **Routing number and sort code checks on the account form never ran.** They were sent under the wrong field name, so only IBAN was checked.
- **A receipt that failed to attach to a new transaction** now shows the warning saying so, where the failure used to go unnoticed.
- **Dropping a category next to one of its own subcategories no longer loses it.** It made the category its own parent, so the whole branch vanished from the list and editing or deleting it could hang. That move is now refused, and categories already caught this way come back at the top level after the update.
- **Resetting your data, restoring a backup or deleting a user no longer leaves other people's data pointing at it.** Their transactions, bills and income stayed filed under your deleted shared categories, their transactions kept your tags, their bills kept auto-paying from your deleted shared accounts and their transfers stayed paired with deleted rows. Those links are now cleared the same way deleting a single category or account clears them, and a recurring pension payment funded from an account that has gone stops auto-posting, where it went on recording payments with nothing leaving any account.
- **Dashboard tiles showing some of your accounts, or filtered by tag, add up properly.** Spending in categories excluded from reports was taken off their totals from every account, including the ones the tile leaves out, so a total could go negative, and a shared category took the other person's spending off yours as well.
- **Removing duplicate categories, or all of them, in Setup takes them off split parts too.** The parts were left filed under a category that no longer existed.
- **Account pickers no longer offer accounts shared with you read-only.** The transaction form, Quick Add, bills, transfers, income, rules, import and reconcile listed them, and saving into one was refused. Imports and bank sync now offer only your own accounts, as importing into an account shared with you always failed. A savings goal can still track one.
- **The number format preview in Settings updates when you change it.** It kept showing the old format and each change logged an error.
- **Typing an amount for a transfer between currencies sends one exchange rate lookup.** It sent one for every time the form had been opened, and a slow earlier reply could overwrite the amount you had just typed.

### Security
- **Undoing a bill payment only removes that payment's own transactions.** It deleted any transaction the request named, including other people's unshared ones.
- **Mark Paid only links transactions in accounts you can change.** It would link any transaction whose id it was sent, including one in an account you couldn't see or one shared with you read-only, and pay the bill with it. Mark Paid now only offers, and only accepts, transactions in accounts you can write to.
- **Ending a share cleans up after itself.** Mark Paid, Skip, undo and auto-pay went on writing to and deleting from the owner's account, the bills' pending transactions stayed in it, and Mark Paid still listed the owner's transactions as possible matches. The other person's own transactions, bills, income and import rules also kept the owner's categories and accounts, so their lists showed names they could no longer see and saving them again was refused. Now, when a share is revoked or left, or accounts or categories are taken off it, those become uncategorised, and bills, income, savings goals and pension payments let go of the account, with auto-pay and auto-post switched off. Their splits with contacts are kept and still count, and sharing again works as normal. A transfer into an account that is no longer shared, has been closed or was removed by its owner's reset is refused with "Edit the bill and choose another account" until another one is chosen, rather than being marked paid with nothing recorded.
- **Deleting a Nextcloud user removes their budget data and shares.** Their bills kept auto-paying into accounts others had shared with them, the people they had shared with kept write access to their accounts, and a new user later given the same user name would have inherited all of it, including the shared expenses other people had linked to them. The removal works for very large budgets on PostgreSQL too, and is all or nothing, so if it fails nothing of theirs is removed and it can be run again, however the access other people gave them is still taken away straight away. Background jobs no longer act for a deleted user either, so data left by users deleted before this version no longer auto-pays into accounts shared with them, and `occ budget:purge-deleted-users` can remove it.
- **A split stops showing a transaction that is no longer shared.** Someone could split a transaction from an account shared with them with a contact linked to another user, who went on seeing that transaction, edits included, after the account stopped being shared. The transaction now shows only while the person who split it can see it. The split itself stays, with its own amount, under its note or "Shared expense", and still counts and can be settled.
- **Sharing a category no longer shows your other accounts.** Its details on the Categories page listed and counted the owner's transactions from all of their accounts, including ones never shared with the person viewing it. They now only cover the accounts that person can see.
- **A transfer no longer names an account that wasn't shared with you.** On an account someone shared with you, a transfer to one of their other accounts showed that account's name in the transactions list, "Transfer → Owner savings", although the account itself was never shared. It now reads "Transfer", as it already did over the API.
- **Names are always shown as text.** Payees and vendors from imports and bank sync, and the names of shared categories and accounts, were put into some lists as HTML, so markup in a name was rendered.
- **Tags in shared categories and accounts.** Someone with write access to one of your shared categories could edit or delete the tags in your other categories. A bill also accepted any tag, so its payments could show another user's tag, and the tag trends report named any tag it was asked about. Bills, and transactions in an account shared with you, now only take tags you can see that the account's owner can use, and the tag picker on such a transaction only offers those and says why when a change is refused.
- **Categories must belong to the ledger.** Transactions, splits, bills, recurring income, import rules and categorising in bulk accepted a category id belonging to another user, and that category's name then showed in the transaction list. Only categories the account owner can see are accepted now, including a bill's or recurring income's own category when it pays from or into someone else's account or is linked to a transaction there, and an import rule with such a category leaves it out when it runs. On an account shared with you, and on a shared bill or recurring income, the category also has to be one shared with you, and the category pickers there only offer those, while a category the row already has stays as it is, even one that isn't shared with you. Its name still shows wherever the transaction does, on the transactions list, the account's page and the dashboard, and the transaction, bill, transfer and recurring income forms show it greyed out as, for example, "Food (not shared with you)". An account that wasn't shared with you is still never named. Over the API, a new transaction with such a category is still recorded, without a category, and the response says why in `category_error`, so a capture is never lost.
